_authored: 2026-08-04, executor session, E08 Task 3 step 2 (Amendment 28 Ruling 3, Amendment 29 ledger 14).
_purpose: Per-view BRUSH prompts for the eight stroke cameras, carrying the full W3 fixture. Replaces texpass_brush.py's stale --prompt default, which must not run.
_what_was_wrong_with_the_default: texpass_brush.py:26-30 carried: 'a burly bald warrior with a long red beard, dark green knitted sleeveless tunic, polished gold pauldrons, GOLD NECKLACE, dark red layered cloth skirt with a leather belt, heavy dark boots, holding a massive greatsword, plain grey background, visible brushstrokes, painterly worked surface'. Measured against canon/W3-IDENTITY.md's sixteen NAMED elements: 8 of 16 present, and one of those eight is the term the fixture STRUCK. Absent: N5 gold scrollwork, N6 the gold belt medallion (the necklace displaced it), N9 green cloth panels, N10 brown leather bracers, N11 the gold forearm plates, N12 gold knee plates, N15 the ornate gold crossguard, N16 the gold pommel. The blade's two named gold elements were both missing from the stage that paints the blade.
_why_this_matters_here_specifically: The brush is the stage that paints everything the reference never reached — measured at eight cameras, 50,569 texels of the blade band have no reference at all (Amendment 28). E07's flesh blade reached the Director THROUGH this stage. The architecture ruling applies without modification: a canon element not named in the prompt is arriving by accident and will leave the same way. N15 and N16 were arriving by accident.
_N7_arrives_as_a_head_noun_now: The default had 'dark red layered cloth skirt WITH A LEATHER BELT' — N7 as a modifier on N8, and missing 'brown'. E08 Amendment 13 measured that elements expressed as modifiers on other nouns are unreliable, and the fixture is written to that rule. 'a brown leather belt' is its own phrase here. Caught while auditing the default against the fixture; folded in per Amendment 29.
_the_spec_is_NOT_view_gated_and_this_is_: Same reasoning as E08-armB-prompts.json, which measured it: E01's face-on-the-back-of-the-head came from a BROKEN CONTROL (Canny returning 6,482 interior edges with no outer contour), not from an unfiltered prompt. Arm B carried the full spec on all eight twins with the exact-silhouette control and NO face appeared on views 3/4/5 — the pre-registered falsifier did not fire. The brush's control is the same geometry. Gating elements out of rear views would remove the thing being tested and make any drift unattributable.
_the_risk_stated_before_the_run: The brush runs at denoise 1.0 INSIDE the mask, so a hole texel has no content to preserve and the model composes freely from prompt plus contour. That is a weaker anchor than the twins' canny-locked restylize. If a beard, a face or a frontal element appears on a rear-camera stroke, that is a REAL failure attributable to carrying the full spec unfiltered at denoise 1.0 — not to the control — and the fix would be view-gating the brush specifically. Recorded here so it cannot be reinterpreted afterwards.
_orientation_phrases: Orientation is not identity, so varying it does not vary the specification. Mapping follows E08-armB-prompts.json: yaws 315/000/045 'seen from the front' | 090/270 'seen from the side, in profile' | 135/225 'seen from behind, at three-quarters' | 180 'seen from directly behind'. The two +55 elevation cameras add 'from above', which is the only new phrase in this file — they are the only cameras that can see the crown, the tops of the pauldrons and the tops of the boots.
_order_is_UNCHANGED_from_the_shipped_def: Byte-identical to texpass_loop.ps1's $default_order. It is stated here rather than inherited so the recipe file carries it (PIN_PER_STEP), and it is NOT re-derived even though stage 1 now covers all eight yaws instead of two — changing the order would be a second variable in a run that already has one. Recorded as an open observation instead: the spiral was designed to start adjacent to two styled poles, and with eight-camera stage 1 the styled region is far more uniform, so the rationale is weaker than when it was measured. Whether the order still matters at 92.9% acceptance is unmeasured.
_negative_is_inherited_and_earned: Byte-identical to E08-armB-prompts.json's negative. The belt terms are not speculative: texpass_loop.ps1's own header records that opening on yaw 90 returned 'a plaited belt, a strap across the upper arm, and a tunic extended to mid-thigh'. Those failure modes were measured at THIS stage, which is what makes the negative earned rather than decorative.
_sidecars: texpass_loop.ps1 passes --prompt per stroke from this file keyed by job name; texpass_brush.py records it in the job sidecar. The version field above is what a later session cites.
_negative: braided belt, plaited belt, woven belt, rope belt, shoulder strap, chest strap, baldric, bandolier, watermark, text, logo, blurry, photo, deformed
